words: Four staged members of the Cottonwood publish function's source-map entry no longer hashed to the entry's recorded sha256 at HEAD. The writer drain ff6c0633a7 changed the publisher and the series contract, and other seats edited two registry files, systems.json and scopes.json. Each stale member now carries as its pin the last commit that changed its file, and as its sha256 the hash of the file at HEAD, which equals the bytes at that pin. The other eight members, the entry's deployed fields (artifact_sha256, last_deployed_commit, last_deployed_at and recorded_by) and every other entry and top-level key are byte-identical to the base. The BUILD_ONLY package was built from the committed tree, and its unpacked handler passed the writer's behaviour check on a fake S3. Not proven: nothing is uploaded or deployed, the deployed bundle is unchanged by this work, and a pinned file edited by another seat after this commit makes the entry stale again.
